On 3 February 2023, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), members of the protective mothers organization staged a protest in front of the National Civil Court of Appeals, in Lavalle street 1220, in San Nicolas neighborhood, to protest against the reunification of a girl with her father, who is was accused of beating the maternal grandmother of his daughter.

On 3 February 2023, in Eldorado (Misiones), residents staged a protest in front of the Eldorado Electricity Cooperative Limited (CEEL) to demand solutions to the frequent cuts in the supply of water and energy. They marched through San Martin avenue, blocking half of the road.

On 4 February 2023, near El Foyel (Rio Negro), a group of people who marched to the Hidden Lake (Lago Escondido) through the Mountain road as part of a protest calling for the opening of a public access to the lake continued to camp in front of the owner's property. The lake had been inaccessible because a multimillionaire had bought the surrounding territories, closing the access to the public. The action took place in the context of the seventh March for Sovereignty of Lago Escondido, and the protesters were part of the Juana Azurduy column. The protesters demanded to return through the Tacuifi road, but they decided to end the protest and left the place through the vehicle access, in the presence of the police.
On 4 February 2023, in Tigre (Buenos Aires), a group of people staged a protest to demand the protection of wetlands and the protection of these spaces from construction works.

On 4 February 2023, in Rosario (Santa Fe), a group of people protested at the National Monument to the Flag to demand justice for the case of a man who was beaten to death in Villa Gesell in 2020. They called for life imprisonment for the eight suspects, demanded the non-repetition of the case and repudiated the racist comments that the perpetrators shouted during the attack.

On 5 February 2023, in Lomas de Zamora (Buenos Aires), a group of people gathered at Presidente Juan Domingo Peron road and at the intersection between Colombres and Monsenor Piaggio streets to remember two victims of traffic accidents and call for justice. The participants wore T-shirts calling for justice and argued that traffic accidents were also homicides. The actions were organized by the group Yellow Stars, which includes victims of traffic accidents.

On 5 February 2023, in Falda del Carmen (Cordoba), residents partially blocked the bridge as part of a protest to demand more security in the area amid recent robberies. They called for more police presence.

On 5 February 2023, in Rivadavia (San Juan), a group of municipal workers blocked the access to a public workroom as part of a protest demanding assurances that they would keep their jobs. There was a report circulating in social media suggesting that many workers would be dismissed, but the authorities denied the information, claiming that it was fake news.

On 5 February 2023, in Rosario (Santa Fe), over 200 people marched as part of a protest demanding justice for the recent killing of a musician who was shot in front of the Newell's stadium. The protesters marched to the stadium where the victim was shot three times and killed after being driven there.

On 6 February 2023, in Mar del Plata (Buenos Aires), hundreds of taxi drivers staged a protest in front of the sports center to demand authorities act against the drivers of digital platforms who work despite a prohibition to do so. They claimed that the authorities were failing to control the activity of companies such as Uber and Cabify.

On 20 December 2024, in San Miguel de Tucuman (Tucuman), workers from the United Mercantile Trade Group protested against the working hours set by the Chamber of Commerce for the days leading up to the end-of-year holidays, which included Sunday, 22 December, as a working day. The protesters rejected the measure and denounced that employers do not properly pay overtime or grant compensatory days off.

notes: On 20 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), members of social, political, and union organizations gathered in Mayo Square to repudiate repression and economic adjustment policies implemented by President Javier Milei's government. This demonstration also commemorated the protests on 19 and 20 December 2001, which were part of a wave of mobilization against the Argentine government during a significant economic crisis. Participants included members of SUTNA, MST, ATE, MTR, PTS, IS, PO, Polo Obrero, ADEMYS, FPDS, the Buenos Aires University Faculty Association (AGD-UBA), the Unified Education Workers' Union of Buenos Aires (SUTEBA), Marabunta, and other organizations, as well as retirees.
On 20 December 2024, in Mendoza (Mendoza), teachers protested against merging schools focused on youth and adult education, citing negative impacts on students and job losses.

notes: On 20 December 2024, in Rosario (Santa Fe), relatives of victims, social and political organizations, and unions marched from San Martin Square to the National Flag Monument to demand justice for the victims of the repression during the December 2001 protests. notes: On 21 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), members of social, human rights, political, and labor organizations gathered in Mayo Square to commemorate the 23rd anniversary of the widespread protests that took place on December 19 and 20, 2001, which led to the resignation of then-President Fernando de la Rua. In addition to remembering those who died during the protests, participants denounced the economic policies of President Javier Milei, the criminalization of protests, and demanded the defense of labor rights, as well as the repeal of the Bases Law and Emergency Decree (DNU) 70/2023. Members of FIT, PO, Polo Obrero, and other groups participated in the demonstration.

On 21 December 2024, in Caleta Olivia (Santa Cruz), members of the Caleta Olivia Municipal Workers and Employees Union (SOENCO) protested outside the City Hall, demanding salary improvements and the opening of dialogue with the authorities.

On 21 December 2024, in Caleta Olivia (Santa Cruz), members of the Polo Obrero protested outside the former Ministry of Labor of the Nation building, demanding genuine work, a year-end bonus, food supplies for community kitchens, and increases in social programs.

On 22 December 2024, in La Plata - Central (Buenos Aires), parents, former students, and teachers of Kindergarten No. 903, located in San Martin Square, protested to repudiate its possible relocation following the approval of a project in the final session of the Deliberative Council aimed at restoring the park.

notes: On 22 December 2024, in Laboulaye (Cordoba), a large group of residents and animal protection organizations marched and protested outside the headquarters of the Departmental Regional Police Unit to repudiate an animal abuse case in which a dog was killed with a hammer by its owner in collusion with others, including the owner's brother, who is a police officer.

On 22 December 2024, in Santo Pipo (Misiones), relatives and friends of a retiree murdered in his home on November 30 marched from a sports complex to the local police station to demand justice. Protesters repudiated the release of three of the four suspects.

On 23 December 2024, in Mendoza (Mendoza), hundreds of teachers and students protested outside the Government House to repudiate the General Directorate of Schools' (DGE) decision to merge schools focused on adult education. Teachers argued that some students attending night classes would not move to nearby neighborhoods to continue their studies due to insecurity. They also claimed uncertainty about their future work locations if the measure is implemented and pointed out issues related to integrating staff from the merged schools.
On 23 December 2024, in Lujan (Buenos Aires), relatives and friends of three victims of gender-based violence marched to the Prosecutor's Office, demanding the perpetrator's arrest and justice.

On 23 December 2024, in San Miguel de Tucuman (Tucuman), relatives of prisoners from precincts 8, 11, 13, and 15, as well as those from the Police Headquarters Jail, protested in Independencia Square after the inmates announced through cell phone videos a hunger strike to demand better conditions for the inmates transferred to the Benjamin Paz prison.

On 23 December 2024, in Rosario (Santa Fe), members of the Retirees' Front protested at the intersection of Cordoba Street and San Martin Avenue against the challenges retirees have faced for years, which have worsened recently. Protesters reaffirmed their rights and denounced that some retirees must choose between eating or affording medication.

notes: On 24 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), more than 4,000 members of MTE, UTEP, CCC, Barrios de Pie, FPDS, and the Evita Movement protested and organized a Christmas dinner. They offered free services, such as haircuts and showers, for more than 4,000 homeless people in front of the National Congress. During this collective action, UTEP members denounced the misrepresentation of statistics presented by the government as evidence of improvements in the social situation.

On 24 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 14 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), vegans protested in the food court of a shopping center in Palermo to defend animal rights and advocate for a plant-based diet.

notes: On 26 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 13 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), workers from the Secretariat of Human Rights and members of ATE protested against the dismantling of the institution.

On 26 December 2024, in Laboulaye (Cordoba), neighbors and relatives of a person who died after being found in critical condition days earlier in the lake at Municipal Park marched from General Paz Square to the courts, demanding justice for the case.

notes: On 27 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 13 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), a large group of members of human rights, political, and labor organizations protested at the former clandestine detention center of the Navy School of Mechanics (ESMA) to defend jobs, the Secretariat of Human Rights, and the Sites of Memory. The demonstration followed reports of planned layoffs in the area by a Secretariat official. Participants in the protest included members of ATE, MST, PTS, the Unified Union of Education Workers of Buenos Aires (SUTEBA), Jubilados Insurgentes, and other organizations. Hours earlier, Grandmothers of Plaza de Mayo, along with other groups, announced the discovery of Grandchild 138 and reaffirmed the importance of the site (former ESMA) as a space for memory.

On 27 December 2024, in San Miguel de Tucuman (Tucuman), motorcyclists providing services through mobile platforms protested and blocked traffic outside the Deliberative Council to defend their labor activities in response to a proposed regulation for the sector. The protest ended following a meeting between representatives of the motorcyclists and Councilman Ernesto Nagle, who agreed to work jointly on a comprehensive project.

On 27 December 2024, in Ingeniero Maschwitz (Buenos Aires), residents protested in front of the Honorable Deliberative Council (HCD) to repudiate installing a bingo hall in the town. The protesters claimed that this type of activity encourages gambling addiction and that its construction would require the removal of trees.

On 28 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 3 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), members of Cromanon Movement, No Repeat Organization, No Oblivion No Forgiveness Group, and 30 December Organization, among others, protested and organized an artistic festival on Bartolome Mitre Avenue to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the Cromanon Republic event hall fire, which occurred on December 30, 2004, and took the lives of 194 people attending a rock concert. Protesters demanded that the site of the tragedy be turned into a space for memory.

On 29 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 3 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), Cromanon Movement, No Repeat Organization, No Oblivion No Forgiveness Group, and 30 December Organization, among others, protested and organized an artistic festival for a second consecutive day on Bartolome Mitre Avenue to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the Cromanon Republic event hall fire, which occurred on December 30, 2004, and took the lives of 194 people attending a rock concert. Protesters reiterated their demand that the site of the tragedy be turned into a space for memory.

On 29 December 2024, in San Carlos de Bariloche (Rio Negro), members of environmentalist and Mapuche organizations protested at the Civic Center against mega-mining and the repeal, 13 years ago, of the province's anti-cyanide law. During the demonstration, participants, including members of the Union de Trabajadores de la Educacion de Rio Negro (UNTER), Pu Pichike Choike, the Mapuche Articulation and Political Construction Space, the Coordinadora del Parlamento Mapuche Tehuelche de Rio Negro, the Piuke Ecological Organization, the Kultrunazo Collective, and the La Teja Cooperative, covered the monument of President Julio Argentino Roca with a black cloth. At the site, the local mayor criticized the demonstration and its participants.

On 30 December 2024, in San Rafael (Mendoza), members of the LGBTQ+ community protested on the 3rd Pride March, from kilometer zero to the front of the Mariano Moreno Library, after passing through the city center and in front of the City Hall, to demand reaffirmation of their rights.

On 30 December 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 3 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), thousands of people gathered on Saenz Pena Street (Comuna 1), between Esmeralda and Suipacha Streets, to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the Republica Cromanon event hall fire, which occurred on December 30, 2004, and took the lives of 194 people attending a rock concert. Participants demanded that a similar tragedy never occur again. They later marched from Mayo Square to the Cromanon Sanctuary (Comuna 3). Protesters also paid tribute to the victims at the Obelisk (Comuna 1).
